title: MT-Bench Judge Consistency Evaluation
description: Multi-turn conversation evaluation for LLM judge consistency, based on MT-Bench (Zheng et al., NeurIPS 2023). Annotators compare two assistant responses in a pairwise setting, rate overall quality on a 1-10 Likert scale, and classify the conversation category.
overview: MT-Bench is a set of challenging multi-turn questions used to study whether a strong language model can stand in for human judges. Zheng and colleagues introduced it at NeurIPS 2023 alongside the Chatbot Arena data.

The benchmark has 80 questions across 8 categories — writing, roleplay, extraction, reasoning, math, coding, STEM, and humanities — each asked over two turns. Human experts then compared model answers to check how often an LLM judge agrees with people.

The released human-judgment data includes roughly 3,000 expert pairwise votes on which of two answers is better, complementing about 30,000 crowd preference conversations. Judges also score single answers on a 1–10 scale.

The Potato config below reproduces the judging task with a pairwise scheme for A/B preference, a Likert scale for answer quality, and a radio for ties, so you can measure judge consistency. Use it to validate an LLM judge or to collect human preferences on your own model outputs.
